elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered still permits termination "by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other", with the notice specifying the Termination Date; the post-edit proviso constrains only "a Termination Date specified by HDI", so the Company retains a free-standing right to terminate the Agreement without cause. There are no Order Forms in this hosting agreement, so agreement-level termination satisfies the disjunctive element.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The retained notice period is ninety (90) days ("upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"); the redline does not shorten the Company's notice to 30 days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 4.1 nor 4.2(a) as rendered contains any refund of prepaid fees; the only money flow on Company termination runs the other way (the Termination Payment to HDI). No pro-rata refund obligation was added.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Added proviso: "provided that a Termination Date specified by HDI shall be the end of the then-current term." This expressly ties HDI's termination effective date to term end, removing any mid-term HDI walk-away.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" — 90 days sits at the top of the 60–90 day band. Although the sentence is embedded in the auto-renewal mechanic, the notice fixes an arbitrary Termination Date and 4.2(a) computes the payment from the twelve months "preceding the Termination Date", confirming a true convenience exit rather than mere non-renewal; the deterministic "Customer convenience termination present: false" result is a keyword artifact (the clause uses "either Party" rather than naming the Company).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Added to 4.2(a): "provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the fees payable by the Company to HDI hereunder for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." The cap is unconditional and applies to the whole Termination Payment, superseding the uncapped Net Sales formula as the operative ceiling.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "provided that a Termination Date specified by HDI shall be the end of the then-current term" — the termination effective date for the Vendor is expressly anchored to the end of the then-current one-year term, which is what this rule requires beyond a bare notice right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — the 90-day notice applies mutually and therefore binds HDI.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the two inserted provisos supply the only two missing fallback terms (HDI term-end-only exit and a three-months-of-fees cap), while the pre-existing mutual 90-day notice already satisfied the two notice elements.

Preferred is not reached: the Company's notice remains 90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Company convenience termination was added. Preferred element 4 is nonetheless met by the HDI term-end proviso.

Deviation status is correct: before the edits HDI could walk away mid-term on a self-selected Termination Date and the Company's exit carried an uncapped Net-Sales-based Termination Payment, both material fallback failures.

Minimality holds. Two surgical provisos; the favourable retained mechanics (the $800,000 deduction, the divide-by-two floor logic in 4.2(b) and the quarterly instalment schedule in 4.2(c)) are untouched, nothing outside the checklist is deleted, and no survival tail, expense language or procedure was added.

Intent preserved: the cap only reduces the amount payable under the retained formula, so the instalment mechanic still functions, and the HDI proviso is compatible with the 90-day notice (HDI must give at least 90 days' notice expiring at term end). No dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence results.

Residual drafting risk to check before sending: the cap refers to "the fees payable by the Company to HDI hereunder", but HDI's compensation in this agreement appears to be Net Sales-linked. If the agreement does not use a defined "fees" concept for amounts payable by the Company, conform the cap to the actual defined compensation term (e.g., "amounts payable by the Company to HDI under Section [x] for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date") so the ceiling cannot be argued to be zero or undefined.
